title: Check what shared code assumes
statement: When content or code is shared or ported between courses or levels, compare their conventions one by one and check what the shared code assumes.
example: A new level's word cards dropped a say-the-word step on 28 of 28 cards that the shipped level used on 12 of 12.
detail: A review that compared every convention of a new level's lessons with the level already shipped found that the new level's word cards silently dropped the say-the-word step, 28 of 28 cards against 12 of 12 (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R5.md`). A later review found a marking prompt that serves every grade hard-coding "a sentence a third grader could say aloud" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-15-R22.md`), and a port of display code assumed a field the new course never had, so its fallback silently produced a worse screen instead of failing loudly (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-21-R8.md`). Otherwise silent departures and wording fixed to one level slip through.
against: Differences the content licenses are not defects: the comparison set aside any difference "licensed by different canon, different genre (continuous Odyssey narrative vs. four" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R5.md`, line 11) or different difficulty.
